98d4d91f9918.text: Crowded HEK293 images make a fluorescence percentage hard to interpret: the denominator is unclear. We measured reporter-associated local contrast around resolvable DAPI objects and recorded every exclusion. The archive contains 25 fields, 12 condition labels and 2,624 eligible objects. Accepted objects cover only 7.1–20.9% of segmented DAPI foreground across receptor conditions. This is an exploratory expression screen, not a measure of transfection efficiency.

b1b625a164b4.text: This page specifies the reproducible pipeline, its control audit and a concrete failure mode: broad field fluorescence and local object contrast can disagree. It links the exact input CSVs, script, parameters and hashes so another team can reproduce or challenge the analysis. Quantitative findings and all acquired images remain in

d93546f3bc26.text: The numerator is the number of eligible DAPI-connected objects whose reporter score exceeds a channel-specific blank threshold. The denominator is all objects passing the same geometric and background rules. An accepted object is not guaranteed to represent exactly one cell; excluded aggregates can contain many cells. Neither fluorescent pixel area nor this selected-object fraction estimates the fraction of all live cells transfected.

d1355ea3c94b.text: GCaMP6f depends on calcium and reporter abundance, so a dim resting endpoint is not an expression-negative control. Time-resolved stimulation is a different measurement.

6827b3b1ad0e.text: We separate original acquisition, computational scoring and display adjustment following reproducible microscopy reporting principles.

fad84531f389.text: HEK293 cells were imaged 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection. The team confirmed 2% PFA fixation followed by DAPI, with no permeabilization; equal exposure within each fluorescence channel across groups; and blank calibration. Identically numbered channels are the same field. The source provides 1–3 fields per condition and no independent biological repeat or live/dead stain.

32dad878729f.text: Holm adjustment is performed separately over the 11 RED and 11 GREEN comparisons: sort raw values, multiply by the number of remaining hypotheses, take the cumulative maximum and cap at1. Absolute effect size is the condition fraction minus the blank fraction in percentage points.

0f5ec959fc6d.text: These are conditional numerical diagnostics under an independent-object model. Objects from the same field share exposure, local density and preparation; multiple fields from one culture are pseudoreplicates for a biological treatment comparison. Moreover, the primary blank helped set the threshold. The nominal p values therefore do not establish biological significance, and the absence of a small p value is not evidence of equivalence. No number of object-level tests replaces an independent transfection.

Under the specified nominal model, eight of ten receptor-labelled RED comparisons fall below Holm 0.05; Or22a and Or98a do not. GREEN has two such comparisons, Orco-only and Or35a. af3649975d3a.text: Pixel area and object positivity show no detectable monotonic agreement across the 12 labels: REDρ=0.19 and GREENρ=−0.09. The pixel-area statistic is a field median above a global threshold; the object statistic pools counts above local-background-subtracted thresholds. Neither can validate the other merely because both are percentages.

4b03da0bd7fe.text: Or98a is the diagnostic case: 99.10% median GREEN area but 0.50% GREEN-positive objects. Its GREEN export clipping is only 0.0002%, with median intensity 39–45 DN. Thus broad elevation above blank, not demonstrated reporter saturation, is the supported observation. A bright background ring can reduce local contrast; testing that explanation requires inspection of signal and ring distributions, raw acquisition and reacquisition at lower density. DAPI clipping and unresolved aggregates are separate, documented problems.

02b24465a0c9.text: The acquired P2 pilot adds a different measurement to the endpoint images: one 96-well HEK293 plate recorded about 72 h after transfection, without G418 selection. Each condition × stimulus has one well. Fifteen repeated readings of a well describe its time course; they do not provide fifteen independent samples.

85edbc3d061b.text: Each test excursion uses the maximum contiguous three-reading mean, divided by the same well’s five-reading F

6c863c5be303.text: , minus one. The corrected metric then subtracts the earlier buffer excursion, which uses a different baseline. Consequently A11’s 11.86% test excursion and 21.48 percentage-point corrected difference answer different questions. H03 illustrates the importance of this distinction: subtracting a −30.08% earlier buffer excursion turns a 1.42% test excursion into a 31.50 percentage-point corrected difference.

290cbde8041b.text: All 32 original exports and 3,840 readings are preserved. The 24 corrected metrics in rows B/C are excluded following the source-reported gain mismatch; numeric gain itself remains unknown. The other 72 values are retained conditionally. Unknown VOC doses, incomplete DMSO vehicle matching, buffer-control excursions and the absence of independent repeats prevent a calibrated detection limit or receptor-specific response classification.

4093d465f1ba.text: The dominant uncertainty is selection: eligible objects retain only 7.1–20.9% of segmented DAPI foreground in receptor conditions. That is a fraction of fluorescent area, not a fraction of cells. Dense regions remain visible in overlays; they cannot be assigned a reliable cell count from these two-dimensional exports. Segmentation has been visually inspected but has not been benchmarked against independently annotated nuclei.

567f96f533bd.text: The next validation set should contain an independently prepared blank, Orco-only and one OR condition; systematic fields spanning sparse and dense areas; raw camera data at documented exposures; and a suitable independent nucleus/viability measure. Blind annotation of sparse, dense and blank fields would permit precision/recall and merge/split-error assessment. A second transfection would begin to test reproducibility; extra images from the existing culture cannot do that.

ef19d63c9f4f.text: The analysis provides an explicit denominator, reproducible calculations and inspectable failure modes. It measures reporter-associated contrast in a selected subset, reveals calibration sensitivity and separates bright field area from local fluorescence. It does not estimate transfection efficiency, biological reproducibility or receptor response.
